[short] skip 'runs bolero run'

! bolero work init doesnotexist
stderr 'bolero: directory doesnotexist does not exist'
bolero env BOLERO_WORK
! stdout .

bolero work init ./a ./b
cmpenv go.work go.work.want
bolero env BOLERO_WORK
stdout '^'$WORK'(\\|/)gopath(\\|/)src(\\|/)go.work$'

! bolero run  example.com/b
stderr 'a(\\|/)a.go:4:8: no required module provides package rsc.io/quote; to add it:\n\tcd '$WORK(\\|/)gopath(\\|/)src(\\|/)a'\n\tbolero get rsc.io/quote'
cd a
bolero get rsc.io/quote
cat go.mod
bolero env BOLERO_MOD # bolero env BOLERO_MOD reports the module in a single module context
stdout $BOLERO_PATH(\\|/)src(\\|/)a(\\|/)go.mod
cd ..
bolero run example.com/b
stdout 'Hello, world.'

# And try from a different directory
cd c
bolero run  example.com/b
stdout 'Hello, world.'
cd $BOLERO_PATH/src

bolero list all # all includes both modules
stdout 'example.com/a'
stdout 'example.com/b'

# -mod can only be set to readonly in workspace mode
bolero list -mod=readonly all
! bolero list -mod=mod all
stderr '^bolero: -mod may only be set to readonly or vendor when in workspace mode'
env BOLERO_WORK=off
bolero list -mod=mod all
env BOLERO_WORK=

# Test that duplicates in the use list return an error
cp go.work go.work.backup
cp go.work.dup go.work
! bolero run example.com/b
stderr 'go.work:6: path .* appears multiple times in workspace'
cp go.work.backup go.work

cp go.work.d go.work
bolero work use # update bolero version
bolero run example.com/d

# Test that we don't run into "newRequirements called with unsorted roots"
# panic with unsorted main modules.
cp go.work.backwards go.work
bolero work use # update bolero version
bolero run example.com/d

# Test that command-line-arguments work inside and outside modules.
# This exercises the code that determines which module command-line-arguments
# belongs to.
bolero list ./b/main.go
env BOLERO_WORK=off
bolero build -n -o foo foo.go
env BOLERO_WORK=
bolero build -n -o foo foo.go

-- go.work.dup --
go 1.18

use (
	a
	b
	../src/a
)
-- go.work.want --
go $goversion

use (
	./a
	./b
)
-- go.work.d --
go 1.18

use (
	a
	b
	d
)
-- a/go.mod --

module example.com/a

-- a/a.go --
package a

import "fmt"
import "rsc.io/quote"

func HelloFromA() {
	fmt.Println(quote.Hello())
}

-- b/go.mod --

module example.com/b

-- b/main.go --
package main

import "example.com/a"

func main() {
	a.HelloFromA()
}
-- b/lib/hello.go --
package lib

import "example.com/a"

func Hello() {
	a.HelloFromA()
}

-- c/README --
Create this directory so we can cd to
it and make sure paths are interpreted
relative to the go.work, not the cwd.
-- d/go.mod --
module example.com/d

-- d/main.go --
package main

import "example.com/b/lib"

func main() {
	lib.Hello()
}

-- go.work.backwards --
go 1.18

use (
	d
	b
	a
)

-- foo.go --
package main
import "fmt"
func main() {
	fmt.Println("Hello, World")
}
